169.text: This is the typical bug in the spisodes where the lying pegs exist. When there is a lying peg, the gripper doesn't do anything because it has no method in policy yet. I think the gripper can grip the one side, either upper side or bottom side. When the gripper lift the peg gripping one side, then the peg will stand up. The gripper lift the lying peg in the middle point. As you know, when the gripper life the peg with its middle point, then the orientation of peg stays and it won't stand up.

218.text: The gripper should grip the one end to make it stand up.

220.text: When there are two round pegs attached, please find the direction of straight line that two center of pegs make. Then the gripper can rotate the angle and match the direction to that line. In this state, the gripper can lower and grip and lift, this won't touch the smaller one, only will touch the bigger one.

This is the hard case. If possible, the gripper consider its pads length and should be careful to grip only one with some pads alignment where only one peg can be gripped.

402.text: Hey, I found the important failure cause. I explained a few times about this kind of cases. This is not observation or movement failure. This is due to calculation difference in very high accuracy. When the gripper calculate the angle, it can control only 4.6 degree at a time. Approximate calculation that excceeds very a little can lead the gripper's pad touch the peg when lowering. So please grant enoughness. Too tight contol makes this failure because of calculation difference at the very high accuracy level due to angle vague control.
